item.title: Polish Foreign Minister Criticizes Trump Over Putin G20 Invite
item.description: US President Donald Trump was wrong to invite his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to this year’s Group of 20 meeting in Atlanta, according to Polish Foreign Minister Radek Sikorski.
item.dc:creator: Wojciech Moskwa

item.title: UK House Prices in Sharpest Drop Since May, Nationwide Says
item.description: UK house prices dropped at the fastest pace since May, according to one of the country’s largest mortgage lenders, in a sign that aspiring buyers are being put off by a surge in borrowing costs.
item.dc:creator: Irina Anghel

item.title: France to Set Out Plan to Narrow Budget Deficit
item.description: France’s government is set to unveil plans to narrow the budget deficit sharply. Ministers will present the details of a €54 billion ($61.2 billion) effort to curb runaway spending and pare the fiscal shortfall to 5% of economic output in 2027 from 5.4% this year. Bloomberg's Caroline Connan reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: A £4 Billion Fuel Windfall Offers Hope For Struggling UK Drivers
item.description: John Healey is set to reap a £4 billion ($5.3 billion) tax windfall from soaring petrol and diesel prices, putting Britain’s chancellor of the exchequer under growing pressure to announce relief for drivers at his upcoming budget.
item.dc:creator: Irina Anghel

item.title: Trump Downplays Diesel Export Ban Over Impact on Other Fuels
item.description: President Donald Trump signaled that his appetite to ban exports of US diesel has cooled given the risk of unintended price spikes, and one of his top deputies indicated Europe might soon put fresh supplies of the fuel on the market.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy, Jeff Mason and Will Kubzansky

item.title: Trump Touts $54B South Korean LNG Plan in Alaska
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Madeleine Dean (D-PA) says the federal government must play a role in regulating artificial intelligence and work to establish guardrails, arguing that competition with China does not give Washington a pass on oversight. Francis deSouza, Scale AI CEO, says comprehensive testing is needed to understand what AI models can do and the risks they pose before determining how to mitigate them. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Debate Needs Evidence, Not Hopes and Fears: deSouza
item.description: Francis deSouza, Scale AI CEO, says comprehensive testing is needed to understand what AI models can do and the risks they pose before determining how to mitigate them. He argues for an evidence-based approach to AI development, saying the debate over moving faster or slowing down should be guided by a clearer understanding of the technology's capabilities and risks. deSouza also says evaluations should cover both frontier and open-weight models. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Dean: Government Must Play a Role in AI Oversight
item.description: Rep. Madeleine Dean (D-PA) says the federal government must play a role in regulating artificial intelligence and work to establish guardrails, arguing that competition with China does not give Washington a pass on oversight. Dean also criticizes President Trump's handling of the war with Iran, saying the administration should bring in experienced diplomats to help end the conflict. She speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says FlyDubai Pilot in Incident Was ‘Perhaps a Terrorist’
item.description: President Donald Trump said a pilot who stabbed a colleague in the cockpit of a FlyDubai flight en route to Israel was “perhaps a terrorist” and said he had spoken to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu about the incident.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason

item.title: Hegseth Picks Musk, Luckey, Gingrich for Warfare Research Unit
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth delivered a sweeping speech to junior officers and enlisted troops, announcing new military commands and projects, including one to be led by Elon Musk, Anduril Industries Inc. founder Palmer Luckey and former House speaker Newt Gingrich to research the future of warfare.
item.dc:creator: Courtney McBride, Jen Judson and Roxana Tiron

item.title: Consumer Groups Press Congress to Probe Scams on Tech Platforms
item.description: A coalition of advocacy groups urged key lawmakers on Wednesday to hold technology companies accountable for alleged scams occurring on their platforms.
item.dc:creator: J.J. McCorvey

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily: PCE Curbs Fed Bets (Podcast)
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
US consumer spending rose in August at the fastest pace in over a year, helping to power the economy through persistent inflation. Inflation-adjusted personal spending climbed 0.6% in August from a month earlier, for the biggest monthly jump since March 2025. The Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of underlying inflation, the personal consumption expenditures price index excluding food and energy, rose a less-than-expected 0.2%. The prior month was also revised lower.
On today's episode:
Mike McKee, Bloomberg News & Lindsey Piegza, Chief Economist at Stifel David Bahnsen, Founder & CIO at The Bahnsen Group Mike McGlone, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Commodity Strategist Jennifer Palmer, Founder & CEO at JPalmer Collective (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says He Raised Case of Hong Kong’s Jimmy Lai With Xi
item.description: President Donald Trump said he discussed the case of imprisoned Hong Kong businessman Jimmy Lai with Chinese leader Xi Jinping during their summit last week, but did not offer details on whether it yielded any results.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason

item.title: AI Safety Measures Widely Backed by Most Americans, Poll Finds
item.description: A vast majority of Americans favor requiring artificial intelligence companies to meet independent safety benchmarks for their models, even if those standards mean slowing development of the technology, according to a new poll.
item.dc:creator: Michael Shepard

item.title: US Consumer Spending Jumps by Most in a Year
item.description: US consumer spending rose in August at the fastest pace in over a year, helping to power the economy through persistent inflation. Inflation-adjusted personal spending climbed 0.6% in August from a month earlier, according to Bureau of Economic Analysis data released on Wednesday. That was the biggest monthly jump since March 2025. We get reaction from Bloomberg's Mike McKee and Lindsey Piegza, Chief Economist at Stifel. Bruce Markets CEO Jason Wallach joins Bloomberg News' Bernard Goyder to discuss the company's role in Robinhood Markets' plan to debut weekend equity trading. Jennifer Palmer, Founder & CEO at JPalmer Collective, discusses the evolving non-bank lending landscape. All on the latest episode of "Bloomberg Businessweek Daily." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Good Economic News May Not Be Enough to Save GOP in Midterms
item.description: Trump and his party find themselves in the same position Democrats did before the 2024 election.
item.dc:creator: Mark Niquette

item.title: How Much Does it Cost to Win The US Senate?
item.description:
Record spending on 2026 midterms is shaping the handful of Senate races that are newly in play for Democrats and will impact the 2028 presidential race.
(Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says Powell Should Be Forced to Resign From Fed Board
item.description: President Donald Trump said former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell should resign from the central bank’s Board of Governors over findings the central bank mismanaged the renovation of its headquarters.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Mason and Enda Curran

item.title: MI5 Accuses Chinese Institute of Spying on UK’s AI Research
item.description: The UK’s domestic security service MI5 accused a Chinese academic institute of spying on Britain’s artificial intelligence research.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham

item.title: India Opposition Plans Nationwide Marches Over Election Row
item.description: India’s opposition parties said they will organize protest marches across the country in October as they step up pressure to remove the top election official over a controversial overhaul of electoral rolls.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Roy and Sudhi Ranjan Sen
